correctness.rationale: For periodic zero-mean b, (C*D_b C)_{jk}=Σ_{n≥max(j,k)} b_n/(n+1)²=O((1+max(j,k))^-2) by bounded partial sums; its Hilbert–Schmidt norm is finite. This yields C*D_|a-µ|² C=v C*C modulo compacts. Weakly-null Hardy extremizing vectors prove ||π(C)||=2, so ||π(D_(a-µ)C)||=2√v. Conjugation by the Calkin shift is a *-automorphism and cyclic averaging annihilates the periodic centered row modulation. Averaging (y+z)*(y+z) for fixed-point z eliminates both mixed terms, giving lower bound 4v for squared distance to the essential commutant. Since C and finite-ranks lie in the Toeplitz algebra, µC+P_ND_(a-µ)C achieves the limiting upper bound. One shift conjugation gives essential commutator 2√δ. Finite averaged variance/tail tests corroborate, not replace, Calkin proof. Full Hardy/Calkin and Sang inclusion explicitly needed.
